In my initial investigation of replacing configure-ovs, I've found some gaps in the NMState capture functionality that are problematic for this work. I'll try to separate them into blockers and woud-be-nice features.

Eventually, all of these will need to be converted to NMState Jira tickets.
h3. Blockers

It does not appear to be possible to capture static IP addresses from at least ipv6 interfaces. It fails with the following error:
{noformat}
Jan 28 21:31:18 master-0.ostest.test.metalkube.org nmstatectl[1615]: NmstateError: PolicyError: Failed to find property address, exists properties are enabled,dhcp,autoconf
Jan 28 21:31:18 master-0.ostest.test.metalkube.org nmstatectl[1615]: | {{ capture.base-iface.interfaces.0.ipv6.address }}{noformat}
Interestingly, this is only a problem with ipv6 addresses. If I only use ipv4 then it works fine. This probably qualifies as more of a bug.
h3. Would-Be-Nice

Support altnames in capture section. I tried to do this, and while it doesn't fail, it also doesn't do the right thing. For example, with enp2s0 having an altname of "primary", if I write a capture rule like "base-iface: interfaces.primary", what I actually get for base-iface.0 is enp1s0. I suspect it may just be matching all of the interfaces rather than just the one with the primary altname.

What I would like to be able to do is something like this:
{noformat}
    capture:
      base-iface: interfaces.primary
    desiredState:
      interfaces:
      - name: {{`"{{ capture.base-iface.interfaces.0.name }}"`}}
        type: {{`"{{ capture.base-iface.interfaces.0.type }}"`}}{noformat}
This isn't as critical because for this use case we could probably just say that you can't have any other altnames on the interface and then we can capture it with interfaces.alt-names.0.name == "primary".

h2. Summary

Add global configurable settings for NNCP retry and exponential backoff strategy
h2. Description
h3. Background

PR #1370 ([https://github.com/nmstate/kubernetes-nmstate/pull/1370]) introduced exponential retry/backoff logic for failing NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy (NNCP) resources. The implementation uses hardcoded constants for the retry and backoff strategy:
{code:go|title=nodenetworkconfigurationpolicy_controller.go (Lines 67-68)|borderStyle=solid}
    MaximumTimeBackoff = 30
    RetriesUntilFail   = 5{code}
Currently, the backoff strategy is:
 * Initial backoff: *1 second*

 * Maximum backoff: *30 seconds*

 * Retry limit: 5 retries (retries until *maximumUnavailableNodeCount* NNCE have failed 5 times ** with the exponential backoff strategy)

This configuration is applied at the controller level using {*}workqueue.NewTypedItemExponentialFailureRateLimiter{*}.
h3. Problem Statement

The current hardcoded retry and backoff configuration cannot be adjusted without rebuilding the operator. Different deployment environments may have different requirements:
 * *Production environments* may need longer backoff periods and more retries for stability

 * *Development/test environments* may need shorter timeouts for faster feedback

 * *Large-scale clusters* may need different retry strategies to balance load and recovery time

 * *Edge/constrained environments* may need reduced retry attempts to conserve resources

h3. Proposed Enhancement

Introduce a *global configuration mechanism* for retry and backoff strategy in the NMState Custom Resource, allowing cluster administrators to tune these parameters according to their environment needs.
h3. Acceptance Criteria
 # API Changes: Add new fields to NMStateSpec:
{code:go}
// PolicyRetryConfiguration defines retry and backoff settings for NNCP reconciliation
   type PolicyRetryConfiguration struct {
       // InitialBackoff defines the initial backoff duration before the first retry
       // +kubebuilder:default:="1s"
       // +optional
       InitialBackoff metav1.Duration `json:"initialBackoff,omitempty"`
       
       // MaximumBackoff defines the maximum backoff duration between retries
       // +kubebuilder:default:="30s"
       // +optional
       MaximumBackoff metav1.Duration `json:"maximumBackoff,omitempty"`
       
       // MaxRetries defines the maximum number of retries before marking an enactment as failed
       // +kubebuilder:default:=5
       // +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1
       // +optional
       MaxRetries int `json:"maxRetries,omitempty"`{code}
Add to NMStateSpec:  
{code:go}
// PolicyRetryConfiguration is an optional configuration for NNCP retry and backoff strategy.
   // If PolicyRetryConfiguration is specified, the handler will use the config defined here instead of its default values.
   // +kubebuilder:default:={}
   // +optional
   PolicyRetryConfiguration PolicyRetryConfiguration `json:"policyRetryConfiguration,omitempty"`{code}

 * Controller Changes:

           Modify {*}controllers/handler/nodenetworkconfigurationpolicy_controller.go{*}:
 * 
 ** Remove hardcoded constants *MaximumTimeBackoff* and *RetriesUntilFail*

 * 
 ** Read retry configuration from the *NMState* CR

 * 
 ** Apply default values if configuration is not specified

 * 
 ** Update the rate limiter initialization in *SetupWithManager* to use configurable values

 * 
 ** Update retry logic in *Reconcile* to use configurable *MaxRetries*
 * Documentation:
 ** Update the release notes to reflect the new configurable fields

 * 
 ** Add examples in *docs/examples/* showing how to configure custom retry settings

 * 
 ** Update user guide documentation explaining when and how to tune these settings
 * Testing:
 ** Add unit tests verifying default values are applied correctly

 * 
 ** Add unit tests verifying custom configuration is respected

 * 
 ** Add E2E tests demonstrating configurable retry behavior

 * 
 ** Ensure backward compatibility (existing clusters without configuration continue working with default values)

 * Validation:
 ** Add validation to ensure MaxRetries >= 1

 * 
 ** Add validation to ensure InitialBackoff < MaximumBackoff

 * 
 ** Add validation to ensure backoff durations are positive

h3. Technical Notes

The implementation should:
 * Access the NMState CR configuration during controller setup

 * Watch for changes to the NMState CR and potentially restart the controller if retry configuration changes

 * Maintain backward compatibility by using the original hardcoded values as defaults

 * Update the event recording logic to reference the configured retry limit instead of hardcoded RetriesUntilFail

 * Update condition messages to reflect the configured values

items.toString:
In principle it would be nice if the nmstate CR allowed you to disable operator pod to deploy network policies in case user manages traffic on their own. On the other hand, once we add such a field to the spec of the nmstate CRD, it needs to stay there forever.

Given that it's not yet clear what Operator SDK will allow us to ship as part of the bundle and what not, I am not yet convinced if having this in the spec of the CRD is going to be the ultimate&elegant solution.

With the current approach where we deploy policies for the operator and handler ourselves from inside the operator pod, the CR can control everything. But once we decide that the general policy for the operator comes from the bundle, then nmstate CR will only control what operator pod deploys after it runs (i.e. additional policies for handler, webook, metrics, console and so on).
